## TL;DR

Kept the 180 ms show delay and 350 ms minimum visible interval at the app shell, as the owner’s release-scope decision requires. Corrected the Settings grouped-row shape and tied non-board placeholder counts to the collections or section definitions that the pages render. Mission Control uses one representative content block, and Stories uses one representative row. Reduced motion disables the skeleton pulse and transition based on the platform preference. Mission Control and Stories loading shots remain removed under the accepted no-loading-screenshots scope.

## Work and rationale

The app shell retains its one-time delay and minimum-visible behavior. After round 2, the task owner explicitly froze the release scope: only shell loading is gated, and independently loaded view and panel skeletons remain immediate pending a follow-up. `PageSkeleton` supports an opt-in `defer` mode, enabled only at the shell call site. In that mode it owns the timers and reports visibility so the shell can retain its wrapper through the minimum interval. Other callers render immediately from their loading state. The shell keeps the exact `<RouterView v-else class="main-route" />` structure required by the shared page-height layout test.

Per-view uses pass the data owner’s loading predicate and collection size, while rendering immediately. Cached data remains visible during background refreshes: detected agents, check runs, scheduled tasks, reminders, provider rows, release channels, and deployment data do not swap back to skeletons. Secrets now seeds its first render from the fresh environment-list cache, including an empty list, so that state does not show a placeholder while revalidating. The empty detected-agent state also remains visible when an empty cached snapshot exists.

The skeleton item-count map was removed. Work and Inputs continue to use the same column constants as their real boards. Settings uses its actual grouped-field section definition, restoring a multi-row shape rather than the single row introduced in the earlier revision. Other view-level skeletons receive counts from the corresponding page arrays or groups: check-plan steps, secret keys, agent cards, release channels, deployment service and branch rows, development targets, check runs, reminders, schedules, provider rows, and detected-agent rows. Where the first-load view has no data from which to infer a collection size, the component renders the named representative-block layout. This keeps the shell placeholder compact without inventing a full list.

Reduced-motion handling reads `prefers-reduced-motion` from `matchMedia`, applies a reduced-motion class, and removes both pulse animation and opacity transition. The listener methods are optional so older browser mocks and environments that only provide the `matches` value continue to work. Each skeleton root is a single polite status region with `aria-busy`; the decorative placeholder rows do not create separate live announcements.

The audit table in the earlier task report remains the inventory of route layouts and their skeleton counterparts. This revision addresses the timing and count issues found during review and preserves the accepted screenshot scope: `Shots` is empty because the capture gate rejects pages that intentionally show `aria-busy`. Component tests provide the evidence for loading-state structure and counts.

## Approaches tried

The initial round 2 fix placed timing inside `PageSkeleton` for every caller, which matched the reviewer’s finding but exceeded the owner’s newly frozen release scope. I kept one implementation of the timing state machine in the component and made it opt-in with `defer`; only `App.vue` enables it. This preserves a single timer implementation for the shell without adding delay to independent views or panels.

For item counts, the earlier version used a per-kind count table. Review correctly pointed out that most values were unrelated to their real data. The revised callers pass lengths from their page collections or the static Settings section definition. The component derives board columns from the live board definitions and otherwise uses the representative-block definition only when a page has no collection available yet. Tests now check both that every call site supplies its loading state and count source, and that the component renders the count implied by its layout kind.

## Challenges and blockers

The full remote suite initially caught a compatibility issue: some tests stub `matchMedia` with a plain `{ matches }` object, so calling `addEventListener` unconditionally threw across unrelated Settings and Agents tests. Making registration and cleanup optional resolved that shared failure. A later owner decision narrowed the timing scope; component tests now exercise deferred shell timing, while per-view callers leave `defer` unset and therefore remain immediate. One empty cached detection case also showed that suppressing the empty state during refresh was incorrect; its predicate now preserves an empty snapshot while revalidating.

The remote validation runner stalled twice before producing a result. RepoOS removed the stalled containers and retried on alternate hosts. The final run completed on Mini with all changed-path tests passing, followed by the local guards. No source files were changed after that successful check; the report draft records that checked tree.

## Key learnings

A timing contract only works when the shell placeholder stays mounted long enough to observe loading turning false. In the shell, `PageSkeleton`’s opt-in deferred mode owns that lifecycle, while the App wrapper keeps the header and route layout stable. View-level skeletons remain immediate under the accepted scope, and each page remains responsible for cached-data decisions and supplying counts from its actual layout.

Counts should express the shape of available content, not how many cards seem visually balanced. Dynamic collections should drive their placeholders, static grouped settings should share their section definitions, and a single representative block is the honest fallback before data exists. Tests for those relationships need to check the page bindings as well as the component’s rendered count; comparing a renderer with its own duplicated count table cannot detect drift.
